name: Neonatal Encephalomyopathy-Cardiomyopathy-Respiratory Distress Syndrome
aliases: Neonatal Encephalomyopathy with Cardiomyopathy and Respiratory Distress

criteria.description: Clinical evidence of neonatal encephalopathy including altered consciousness and seizures
Echocardiographic confirmation of cardiomyopathy (dilated or hypertrophic) in the neonatal period
Severe respiratory distress syndrome requiring mechanical ventilation within the first week of life
Laboratory evidence of metabolic derangements such as elevated lactate or abnormal acylcarnitine profile
Identification of pathogenic variants in mitochondrial or nuclear genes associated with combined encephalomyopathy and cardiomyopathy

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of all three major criteria: neonatal encephalopathy, cardiomyopathy, and respiratory distress syndrome within the neonatal period
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical supported by imaging, laboratory, and genetic testing; exclusion of other causes is essential.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Neonatal onset altered level of consciousness
Dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy diagnosed by echocardiography
searchTerms: heart muscle disease seen on echo

pathognomonic.symptomName: Severe neonatal respiratory distress requiring mechanical ventilation

common.symptomName: Feeding difficulties with poor suck reflex
searchTerms: poor feeding due to weak sucking reflex
big heart detected by chest imaging

laboratory: Elevated blood lactate and pyruvate levels
Metabolic acidosis on arterial blood gas
Abnormal acylcarnitine and organic acid profiles
imaging: Echocardiogram showing dilated or hypertrophic cardiomyopathy
Brain MRI demonstrating diffuse white matter abnormalities and basal ganglia involvement
Chest X-ray showing cardiomegaly and pulmonary congestion
genetic: Pathogenic variants in mitochondrial DNA or nuclear genes affecting mitochondrial function (e.g., POLG, TK2)
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating mitochondrial abnormalities (if performed)

distinguishingFeatures: Stroke-like episodes typically after neonatal period
Predominantly neurological symptoms without early cardiomyopathy
Presence of infectious markers and positive cultures
Absence of primary cardiomyopathy and mitochondrial dysfunction

redFlags: Rapid progression of cardiomyopathy with heart failure signs
Refractory seizures despite standard anticonvulsant therapy
Severe respiratory failure unresponsive to conventional support
references: Mitochondrial Medicine Society: Consensus Statement on Diagnosis and Management of Mitochondrial Disease
Recent Advances in Neonatal Cardiomyopathy and Encephalopathy, Journal of Pediatrics, 2024
